edge_explainer: SELF-CORRECTION RECORDED. This court's first draft argued the 9.8x EV/EBIT was an artifact of a recurring add-back that had grown five-fold and would keep recurring, implying ~21x statutory. Primary sources REFUTE that: FY2023 non-recurring items were only GBP 82k, the FY25 GBP 5,881k is overwhelmingly one item (closure of Glasson Dock and Standon Mill, GBP 4,137k, plus GBP 1,744k reorganisation), the 1-Dec-2025 TU guided its NET CASH cost to only GBP 2.0-2.5m after asset realisations, and H1 FY26 (to 30-Apr-2026) had ZERO non-recurring items. This is a genuine, bounded, mostly non-cash three-year transformation charge cycle (Project Genesis, launched Feb-2025, completes 2027), not chronic adjusted-inflation. The add-back is defensible and my draft was wrong. The decline stands on different grounds: GBP 583m of revenue producing ~GBP 9-10m of operating profit is a 1.6% EBIT margin and ~5% ROE - a low-return distributor that does not fit a quality-at-own-history-discount frame; there is no drawdown to court (-0.6% over a year, 52-week low 251 days old); the consensus recovery is already priced; and a 408bp touch with a 300-share NMS makes it unownable at our size.
